description: Exports then vacuums the systemd journal (CPU, boot and service logs). The export is a snapshot for inspection, not a restorable backup.

fields.name: Scope
fields.label: Which journal
fields.helpText: system vacuums the machine journal (needs root via polkit); user vacuums your own journal (usually unprivileged, but root-owned files under /var/log/journal may still need elevation).
fields.helpDetail: The Windows version cleared every event log as admin; the Linux default Scope=system is the equivalent and requires elevation through the app. Dry-run preview never needs privilege. Per-volume or remote journals are out of scope.

fields.name: VacuumTime
fields.label: Keep entries newer than
fields.helpText: Journal entries older than this are exported, then vacuumed. Use a number with a unit: 7d, 2 weeks, 365 days (a bare number is read as days).
fields.helpDetail: Normalized to an explicit unit before journalctl --vacuum-time, so preview and vacuum always agree (a bare number becomes '<N> days' — journalctl alone would read seconds). The same value classifies boots in the dry-run preview. Invalid or out-of-range values fall back to 7 days with a warning.

fields.name: VacuumSize
fields.label: Keep total under
fields.helpText: Optional cap on journal disk use (e.g. 500M). Empty means no size cap.
fields.helpDetail: Passed to journalctl --vacuum-size. Size-based deletion cannot be previewed per boot and is not covered by the pre-vacuum export window the way time-based deletion is — the export covers the VacuumTime window.

fields.name: BackupDir
fields.label: Export backup folder
fields.helpText: Pre-vacuum journal exports land here. A failed export aborts the run before any vacuum.
fields.helpDetail: Like the Windows version's rule of never clearing what wasn't backed up: if the export fails (or the folder cannot be created), the run stops with an error and nothing is vacuumed. Exports are `journalctl -o export` snapshots for inspection — they cannot be re-imported the way .evtx files can.
